diagnosis.summary: When warranty@v2 was published updating the warranty from 1 year to 2 years, the obsolete warranty@v1 was not de-indexed. As a result, both warranty@v1#0 and warranty@v2#0 were retrieved and presented to the LLM, causing it to mention the outdated 1-year policy alongside the current 2-year policy.

evidence.claim: warranty@v1 remained indexed with 1/1 chunks even after warranty@v2 was published.
warranty@v2 was published updating the warranty duration to 2 years, with 2/2 chunks indexed.
The retrieve step returned both outdated chunk warranty@v1#0 and current chunk warranty@v2#0.
warranty@v1#0 contains the outdated 1-year limited warranty policy.
warranty@v2#0 contains the active 2-year limited warranty policy.

ruled_out.reason: The configuration change only increased max_response_tokens and did not alter retrieved chunks or knowledge base indexing.

diagnosis.suggested_fix: De-index warranty@v1 so that only chunks from the current version (warranty@v2) are indexed in the knowledge base.

candidates.rationale: Both warranty@v1 and warranty@v2 are simultaneously indexed in the knowledge base, leading the retriever to return outdated warranty policy chunks alongside current ones.
The retriever does not filter out obsolete document versions or properly prioritize latest versions, surfacing superseded warranty@v1 chunks.
The model unnecessarily included contradictory details from the older warranty version instead of strictly stating the active 2-year warranty policy.
